ended: Lost the West 1st Round 2-4 to LAL

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (glass-first)
archetype.definition: A 52-win team with a top-six net rating that ruled the boards all year, then lost its first-round series to the Lakers when its shooting fell apart and its All-NBA scorer appeared in only one game.

report.headline: Same 52 wins, better margin, and a first-round exit with Durant in one game

recap.finish: 52-30, second in the Southwest; lost the West 1st Round 2-4 to LAL
recap.body:
Houston's identity didn't change: it was the league's best rebounding team by a distance and a top-six defense that played slow. It grabbed 34.8% of its own misses, first in the league and nearly nine points above average, and its 54.9 REB % also led the league. The offense finally caught up to the defense. A unit that ranked 13th last year climbed to 8th at 118.6 ORtg, and the Net Rtg rose from 4.5 to 5.4. The record stayed exactly where it was, 52-30 both years. The margin says this was the better team. Its differential implied 54 wins, and the W vs Pt Diff of -2 means close games took a couple away.

The season came in three parts. An 11-2 November set the tone and left them 13-4. After that came a long, ordinary middle: 7-6 in December, then a January in which scoring dropped to 107.88 a game and the defense had to carry them to 10-7. February and March were winning months, but not by much. Then the offense came back. Houston went 9-1 over its last ten with a +15.2 margin per game and closed April 6-1. Through all of it the longest losing streak was three games, so the team never slumped badly. It still finished ten games behind San Antonio in the division.

The engine was Kevin Durant. He put up 2,026 points on 64.1 TS %, made All-NBA Second Team and ranks second among small forwards on the site, and that is most of why the wings grade an A+. Amen Thompson was the other pillar. He produced 10.3 Win Shares, and the team was 5.5 points better with him on the floor. Alperen Şengün made the All-Star team with 1,466 points and 445 assists. Oddly, the team's net rating was better with him off the floor (-5.7 On-Off), and the same was true of Reed Sheppard (-4.4), even though Sheppard hit 227 threes. The defense took away opposing guards. Point guards' points, rebounds and assists combined fell further below their usual output against Houston than against any other defense.

The flaws were familiar ones. Houston took threes on only 35% of its shots, 28th in the league, and turned it over more than most (13.3 TOV %, 23rd). Offensive rebounds and Durant's shotmaking covered for both in the regular season. In the playoffs Durant played one game, and nothing covered for them. The Rockets dropped the first two in Los Angeles by 9 and 7, then lost Game 3 at home 108-112 in overtime. They answered with a 115-96 home win and a 99-93 road win. Game 6 was a 78-98 home loss that ended the season. Over the series they shot a 46.7 eFG % and 30.2% from three, both near the bottom of the postseason field, and averaged 98.67 points.

The defense held up. It forced turnovers at the best rate of any playoff team (16.8 Opp TOV %), and Tari Eason (+17.1 On-Off, 4.0 BPM) and Thompson (+30.9) were excellent. The young shooters were not. Sheppard's TS % fell to 40.7, and the bench forwards were played off the floor. This exit came in the first round, as last year's did, and with one fewer playoff win.

highlights.title: Best rebounding team in basketball
highlights.body: Houston led the league in ORB % and REB %, and the offensive rebounding number sat nearly nine points above the league average. It has climbed for three straight seasons, so this is a built-in trait of the roster, not a fluke. Second chances made up for an offense that didn't shoot many threes, and the edge partly survived the playoffs, where Houston ranked second in ORB %.

highlights.title: Durant's efficient, All-NBA scoring load
highlights.body: Durant scored 2,026 points on 64.1 TS % at a 27.1 usage. That efficiency, at that volume, lifted the offense from 13th to 8th and earned him All-NBA Second Team. He alone accounts for the A+ wing grade, since the other listed wings barely played.

highlights.title: Amen Thompson, two-way centerpiece
highlights.body: Thompson led the backcourt with 10.3 Win Shares, and the team was 5.5 points better per 100 possessions with him playing. He carried that into the playoffs at +30.9. He was the clearest positive across both halves of the season, and guard defense keyed by the backcourt was a major reason Houston's defense ranked sixth.

lowlights.title: Playoff shooting collapsed against the Lakers
lowlights.body: Houston's 46.7 eFG % and 30.2% from three ranked 15th of 16 playoff teams, and it was held under 100 points in four of six games, bottoming out at 78 in the elimination game. Sheppard's TS % fell to 40.7. The low three-point volume that ranked 28th in the regular season left little room to shoot out of a slump.

lowlights.title: Wing group was one player deep
lowlights.body: The A+ wing grade belongs to Durant. Behind him, Jae'Sean Tate and Isaiah Crawford posted negative BPMs and bad on-off numbers in limited minutes. With Durant in only one playoff game, the group produced almost nothing. That thin depth behind the star is the roster's clearest structural weakness.

lowlights.title: Turnovers and a middling frontcourt
lowlights.body: A 13.3 TOV % ranked 23rd, worse than last year's 11.8. The frontcourt graded only B- despite an All-Star center. Jabari Smith Jr. had a -0.7 BPM and Eason a 51.4 TS % over the regular season, and the team's net rating was worse with Şengün on the floor than off. The defense also slipped from 4th to 6th.

arc.note: An 11-2 November gave way to a long stretch of narrow winning months and a January in which the scoring dipped. A 9-1 closing run then led into a first-round loss in which the offense never showed up.

recap.nextYear: The underlying numbers are better than the identical record suggests. Net Rtg rose to 5.4, the offense climbed to 8th, and the margin implied 54 wins, so the 52-30 wasn't inflated by close-game luck. The rebounding edge has grown three years running and should carry over, as should a top-six defense built around Thompson. The questions are about shape, not talent. The A+ wing grade is one player, and the playoffs showed what happens without him. The team still shoots too few threes and turns it over too much for a team trying to win in the postseason. Sheppard and Şengün posted negative on-off numbers despite big counting stats, so the lineups around them need sorting out. Last year's 52 wins brought three playoff wins and this year's brought two. Until the half-court offense can win playoff games without Durant scoring, this group projects as a strong regular-season team that is vulnerable in a series.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus a six-game series. Playoff shooting numbers are a small sample, and Durant appeared in only one game.
